title: "System Architecture and Ownership"
subtitle: "Which layer owns each Runtime responsibility?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** the dev24 responsibility and lifecycle target is `CONVERGING`,
implementation is in progress. Numerical meanings remain unchanged. The single
[Runtime lifecycle contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#package-lifecycle)
owns Run state, operation leases, fixed lazy Results, bounded recovery and native
supervision. This page describes its module handoffs, not a second policy.
Existing dev23 WIP is candidate input; historical observations are not relabelled.
Schematic completion remains incomplete and deferred.

## Organize Python by responsibility

The goal is one understandable implementation with coherent ownership and
dependencies. Preserve documented public imports, signatures, singleton
identities, physical and numerical behavior, failure contracts, canonical
schemas, stored data, and the existing `_julia` and `_schemas` resources.
Internal modules may move and large modules may be decomposed without adding a
second implementation or a compatibility fallback.

| Implementation owner | Responsibility | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| `authoring/` | Components, assembly, capture, parameter point and Plan sealing | Immutable snapshot and resolved parameters |
| `specs.py` | Numerical, Optimization and presentation declarations | Resource-free declarations with deferred presentation imports |
| `compilation/` | Lowering, discretization, coordinates and View realization | Immutable compiled model and realized View, independent of Workspace |
| `numerics/` | JAX assembly, sparse solves and quantity algorithms | Numerical values or existing typed failures; no storage authority |
| `execution/` | Request, operation, CMA ordering, backend transport and resources | Ordered outcomes and evidence publication handoff |
| `workspace/` | Binding, SQLite mechanism, evidence, checkpoint, short reads and bounded recovery | Fixed verified evidence selection |
| `results/` | Typed decoding, exact selection and lazy access | Detached immutable values and minimal reader metadata |
| `diagnostics/` | Optional operation timing and resource observations | Bound diagnostic projections, not numerical success |
| `benchmark/` | Current readonly public operation Benchmark facade | Diagnostic queries and presentation; no experiment execution |
| `visualization/` | Schematic, numerical plots, HTML and reports | Presentation from frozen authoring or typed Results |

These are target responsibilities; active compiler/numerics/CMA/storage code
currently under `benchmark/` must move before obsolete experiment paths are
removed. No empty abstraction hierarchy, parallel implementation, compatibility
wrapper or numerical redesign is implied.

Public modules such as `runtime.py` and `specs.py` remain facades with their
existing imports and interfaces. Converting `authoring.py` and `results.py`
into packages preserves their existing public module paths through explicit
package exports. Other existing public entry points continue to expose their
documented names. Public reexports are legitimate interface boundaries, not
duplicate production authorities. The public `units.py` retains the one Pint
registry, and `io.py` retains its bounded external-artifact ingestion interface.

| Surface before the split | Current responsibility |
|---|---|
| `CircuitRun`, `NetworkViewRef` and public Specs | Retained public names; Run delegates captured binding, request and operation work, with optional `close()` |
| Public numerical Results and `BenchmarkResult` | Retained names; fixed selected evidence and readonly diagnostic reports respectively. `BenchmarkResult.workspace` is the explicit operation-store locator; `BenchmarkResult.open(benchmark.workspace)` reopens that store, not the enclosing Workspace root. |
| Experimental `BenchmarkSpec`, comparison arms and native benchmark executable | Removed experimental execution surface; normal Run operations are the execution authority |
| Internal `benchmark.compiler`, `mesh`, `views` and numerical backends | Replaced by `compilation`, `numerics` and the execution adapter; no old-path compatibility reexports |
| Internal benchmark storage, checkpoint, optimization and timing modules | Replaced by Workspace, execution and diagnostics owners respectively |

Internal relocation is not a second public execution mode. Retained public
reexports point to one implementation; removed experiment modules do not remain
as fallback paths. The CLI has no package console-script entry point or
`scnsim.__main__` service. Packaged Julia request resources remain necessary for
the optional native backend; removing its experimental comparator does not
remove the native request protocol.

Shared code has a named responsibility rather than a generic `core` owner.
Root `canonical.py` owns canonical representation and identity primitives;
workspace artifact verification belongs to `workspace/`, and catalog source
identity belongs to `authoring/provenance.py` with notebook recovery in
`authoring/notebook_source.py`. Shared immutable numerical retention lives in
`value_storage.py`, usable by authoring, Specs, and Results. Moving that helper
does not merge distinct
snapshot freezing, parameter copy-on-read, and immutable bytes-backed array
behaviors. Shared helpers must not acquire a Run, mutable Plan authority,
workspace lifetime, or presentation dependency.

### Decompose authoring at state and representation boundaries

Authoring separates handles, catalog-created components, catalog factories,
parameter declarations, physical value models, and captured-point resolution.
The former large authoring module separates these additional boundaries:

- **Assembly (`authoring/assembly.py`):** shared scope grammar, occurrence overlays, completeness and
  ownership checks, inline Subsystems, and reusable Composite construction.
  Operations that maintain the same wire-equivalence, exposure, and consumption
  invariants remain together.
- **Root Plan (`authoring/plan.py`):** root Ports, Run-preparation and sealing lifecycle, traversal
  required by assembly consumers, and convenience delegation to capture,
  resolution, and rendering.
- **Capture (`authoring/capture.py`):** deterministic net naming, physical occurrence records,
  parameter-consumer closure, and source-unit provenance. It consumes the live
  Plan and produces the immutable handoff; it does not become a second physical
  authority.
- **Snapshot models (`authoring/snapshot.py`):** immutable normalized representation, independently
  consumable without live assembly, execution, or rendering state.

Capture currently completes assembly and establishes the root-owned net
identity map before constructing records. Extraction preserves that order and
the root's ownership of the map. It must not silently redefine capture as a
pure operation. Catalog factory context and construction tokens retain one
authority across modules. Existing public class module identities and reserved
builtin catalog provenance remain intact when definitions move; facade exports
alone do not preserve those identities.

### Preserve dependency direction and lifetimes

Authoring values and immutable handoffs sit below execution and visualization.
Captured-point resolution consumes shared physical domains without importing
diagram code. Authoring rendering conveniences delegate lazily; numerical
imports and execution do not require rendering success. Results consume
verified evidence, and visualization consumes typed values or captured
structure. Pure presentation composition does not allocate attempts, run a
process, mutate a Plan, or publish workspace evidence.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Public["Public facades: authoring, runtime, specs, results"]
    Plan["Authoring: one physical Plan"]
    Snapshot["Immutable snapshot and resolved point"]
    Prepared["Execution: immutable prepared analysis"]
    Process["Execution: selected backend and owned native supervisor"]
    Evidence["Workspace: verified receipts and artifacts"]
    Results["Results: typed values and lazy access"]
    Visual["Visualization: diagrams, plots, reports"]
    Shared["Shared primitives: units, canonical, value_storage"]
    Public --> Plan
    Public --> Prepared
    Plan --> Snapshot
    Snapshot --> Prepared
    Prepared --> Process
    Process --> Evidence
    Evidence --> Results
    Results -. "reacquire and verify original binding" .-> Evidence
    Results --> Visual
    Snapshot --> Visual
    Shared -.-> Plan
    Shared -.-> Prepared
    Shared -.-> Evidence
    Shared -.-> Results
```

The arrows show runtime handoffs and shared dependencies, not a second
orchestrator. `execution/compilation.py` owns compiler-only inspection;
`execution/coordinator.py` owns terminal attempt orchestration and delegates
transport to `execution/process.py`. Result reconstruction lives in
`results/decode.py` and its family decoders. Plot selection helpers live in
`results/selection.py`; they do not import the renderer. Derived numerical
presentation lives in `visualization/plots/`, while schematic realization
lives in `visualization/diagram/`. Reports remain pure composition of verified
typed values.

Runtime coordinates the flow through immutable declarations rather than
passing a mutable Run as shared context. Workspace verification remains the
authority for stored evidence, including immediate decode under its owned
interval and lazy reads after reacquiring the exact original binding. A
relocated check remains necessary when it protects a distinct lifetime or
trust boundary. Remove duplicated checking only when the surviving mechanism
preserves that boundary and its failure behavior; this reorganization does not
authorize new scientific restrictions or changed failure semantics.

### Review the resulting responsibilities

Review explains concrete dependencies, state lifetimes, and representative
flows. It assesses responsibility cohesion, understandable dependency
direction, one state and evidence authority, functional correctness, and
whether an extension has an understandable home. Decomposition is
proportionate when it separates responsibilities that change independently
without scattering one invariant across modules or introducing forwarding
machinery with no ownership purpose. There are no file-length, module-count,
score, or numerical-threshold criteria.

Source inspection supports architectural findings; it does not establish
execution or delivery claims. The authorized implementation checks observe
installed-wheel imports and resources, recursive source identity, real Direct
and pump-off HB execution, exact resolve without a new process, existing
parameter and optimization workflows, checkpoint/recovery and lazy reads, and
fresh native diagram, numerical-plot, and report artifacts. Required CI,
privacy review, and exact target reconciliation remain delivery obligations.
No new durable tests or broader validation workflow are introduced by this
page. Historical course outputs retain their execution bindings and are not
fresh execution evidence; their source-tree transition is separate from
redrawing artifacts.

The subsequent slimming candidate removes implementation without a current
consumer and repeated work within existing owners. Parameter resolution
acquires each detached mapping once, retaining its first-read validation
order; sweep selection similarly caches requested-value encoding only when
the comparison is reached. Wire validation compares retained root identities
without invoking value equality. Preparation retains declaration validation
and encoded requests without unused bound-object storage. Process callbacks
remain immediate, while checkpoint and ledger history remain durable;
discarded volatile progress accumulation is removed. The live JSON pair
decoder, reserved control recognition, canonical validation, geometry checks,
coupling reconstruction, certification, and explicit old-guide refusal remain
their existing authorities. Removed diagram parser islands and discarded box
records have no role in that current path. Julia artifact metadata uses one
builder while preserving existing serialization and numerical algorithms.

These are source observations. Final installed-wheel, native, recovery,
rendering, and independent-review observations remain separate evidence;
source slimming does not itself establish them. Distinct trust lifetimes,
public protocol hooks, and failure stages remain necessary even where code
looks similar.

The current delivery endpoint is a history-preserving develop-to-main PR
promotion followed by exact main/develop/tracking/checkout synchronization,
required CI and Pages outcomes, and privacy review. The current Human-authorized
Alpha promotion and publication prepare exactly `1.0.0a2`; its research exception
does not constitute a stable release or acceptance of CONVERGING semantics.
The immutable first-Alpha snapshot remains historical authority. Publication is
a separate delivery action; parent-repository pins, consumer migrations,
dependency changes, numerical algorithms and data-format changes remain outside
this bounded default-policy amendment.

## Keep the Notebook boundary in Python

Python owns every user-facing object and every trust boundary that benefits
from ordinary Python discovery:

- component authoring, units, Specs, Refs, Runs, and typed Results;
- dimensional validation and canonical serialization;
- workspace locking, request/attempt discovery, receipt verification, and
  exact `resolve()`;
- AEDT Q2D parsing; and
- Plotly numerical presentation and Matplotlib/Schemdraw diagram presentation.

`CircuitRun.build_report()` is the validation facade for already verified
Results. It delegates closed `ReportPanel` selections to a pure report
composer that owns no Run, workspace, process, or execution callback. The
composer reuses the same Plotly presentation layer as standalone numeric
Results; HTML assembly adds only derived presentation identity.

Run construction is also a Python ownership boundary. Python prepares and
validates one captured Plan snapshot and the original View before it publishes
a workspace pointer. The pointer update is the logical commit; the supplied
Plan is sealed from that already-validated state only after commit. A bounded
maintenance record, not a background task, owns cleanup of a replaced leaf.

Julia never imports Notebook objects or calls a Python objective callback. It
receives one sealed request and owns the numerical work inside that request:
component realization, candidate compilation, reduction, Direct quantities,
CMA-ES, and HB.

The backend remains one `SCNSimBackend` module and one reachable engine. Its
source is included in dependency order: wire encoding, physical compilation,
View realization, shared Direct quantity kernels, Result artifact writing,
Direct terminal quantities, terminal/process orchestration, and Optimization.
The existing structured compiler is included inside the compilation owner;
HB and batch execution remain downstream consumers after these eight shared
owners. This file split assigns maintenance responsibility only. It introduces
no Julia namespace, alternate dispatch path, protocol version, numerical
formula, failure rule, or execution boundary.

Optimization alone has one bounded mid-process publication boundary. The Julia
optimization owner freezes completed baseline content and waits; the Python
execution/workspace owner independently verifies and atomically publishes the
request-owned checkpoint before acknowledging it. Julia cannot start a CMA
generation before that acknowledgement. The checkpoint owns recovery content,
the publisher seal owns provenance, and neither becomes a Result or a second
execution engine.

```text
Notebook
  -> Python validation and immutable prepared analysis
  -> canonical request encoding
  -> one external Julia process
  -> independently validated staged outcome and artifacts
  -> receipt seal and verified-success evidence
  -> verified typed Python Result decoding
```

`CircuitRun` is the façade for these owners, not their shared mutable context.
It validates that public Refs and selector Views belong to the captured Run,
resolves parameter declarations once, and produces a private immutable
`PreparedAnalysis`. That record contains only finalized declarations,
normalization, source-unit evidence, and runtime identity. It contains no Run,
workspace, process callback, or executable context. The canonical encoder
formats that prepared record and never selects a View or resolves parameters a
second time.

Execution coordination owns attempt allocation, the one terminal process,
closed outcome validation, and receipt promotion. It returns only verified
workspace success evidence. A separate decoder reconstructs typed Results from
that evidence and the captured identity lookup; it cannot authorize a payload
that the workspace verifier did not accept. Immediate path-backed decoding
stays inside the same ownership-checked reader or writer interval. A lazy sweep
reacquires the original binding's read lock and revalidates the exact request,
attempt, receipt, and Result seals before validating and reading only the
requested chunk or point payload; it neither rescans the whole batch nor
attaches to a replacement leaf. Already materialized detached values may
outlive that interval. This responsibility split does not change request bytes,
algorithms, process count, or public methods.

`run.explain()` and a compiled schematic may use the same Julia compile
preflight, but neither launches a solver nor writes the evidence workspace.

The `CONVERGING` Parameter System keeps this boundary: one ordered
`ParameterSpace` operation is one request and one Julia process, not one
process per point or a persistent service. Values are runtime data; compatible
topology preparation may be reused, but every parameter-dependent assembly and
calculation is recomputed. Exact target behavior belongs to the
[Parameter System Contract](../contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-operations).

## Same-process CPU execution and read-only Benchmark

The dev11 [backend contract](benchmark-and-backends.qmd) and
[usage guide](../guides/benchmark.qmd) describe the `CONVERGING` current candidate.
Normal Run operations default to same-process JAX using the existing Python
physical lowering, View realization, continuation and CMA authorities. Explicit
Julia retains the native process path described above; that path is no longer
the default for supported Direct/root/response and corresponding Optimization.
The Plan leaf owns verified typed Results and checkpoints for either backend.

The base requires Python 3.12 and pinned CPU JAX/CMA dependencies. Initialization
remains lazy and Julia discovery optional. Resolve and operation Benchmark remain
read-only; the latter aggregates parented spans and numerical references without
launching an independent comparison task. Historical dev10 comparison files
retain their original identities; current readers do not support those older
operation Workspaces. Use a new Workspace and recompute. CUDA, ROCm and
Apple GPU execution are outside this Goal.

## Keep the runtime dependency boundary explicit

The reopened [assembly contract](../contracts/circuit-plan-assembly.qmd)
separates three consumers: Parameter, Calculation, and ASCDLS. Shared immutable
assembly, units, and physical values sit below them. Diagram public reexports
and diagram-spec validation load diagram modules lazily without changing public
names. Pure `authoring/resolution.py` resolves a frozen snapshot and
`ParameterSet`, while `authoring/physical_values.py` owns shared physical field
validation. CircuitPlan convenience delegates and Runtime uses its own
frozen snapshot directly. No numerical operation depends on rendering success, and
compiled diagrams remain one-way evidence consumers.

The base package uses Pint, NumPy, Zarr, Plotly, Matplotlib and Schemdraw.
CPU JAX/CMA and sparse numerical dependencies belong to the base package.
The optional `julia` extra supplies JuliaPkg discovery support. Julia-backed
features require a separately provided Julia 1.12.6; feature calls never acquire
its executable. Its internal Julia project uses JSON3, CMAEvolutionStrategy,
JosephsonCircuits, and Julia standard libraries. The lockfile and committed
Julia project/Manifest are the executable dependency authority; this page
explains their ownership boundary rather than defining alternate versions.

SCNSim retains its Plan-leaf SQLite store and backend-specific native artifacts.
It does not add an ORM, external database service, distributed runner, JuliaCall
or persistent daemon. Operation supervision and short storage transactions have
distinct ownership; canonical bodies remain one numerical authority.

## Preserve provenance without inheriting the old product

The legacy Circuit Workbench remains historical implementation provenance. It
does not own SCNSim names, workspace layout, public API, consumers, or release
train. Reusable algorithms are admitted only through the classified matrix in
[External Inputs and Delivery](external-inputs-and-delivery.qmd#legacy-adoption-matrix).

## Sparse CPU numerical foundation (dev13 candidate)

The CONVERGING dev13 implementation replaces the JAX dense nodal path with
immutable indexed local stamps, candidate-specific sparse View congruences and
JAX numeric assembly followed by CPU CSC SuperLU. The source candidate now implements this path; installed-wheel observations
remain pending. There is
no selectable dense numerical fallback. Dense conductor, Port, selected Schur
and actual RHS blocks remain where the mathematics requires them; genuine fill
is preserved without dropping small values.

Compiler and View own binary64 SI lowering and declaration order. The backend
owns requested arithmetic precision, local frequency assembly, direct factors,
analytic derivatives and existing numerical certificates. C/K/G are coalesced
before their separate absolute bounds; each series-RL section is bounded before
section summation. Host continuation/CMA and Workspace commit/checkpoint
authorities remain separate. The private Python-to-Julia transport may materialize
a dense descriptor at that adapter boundary; explicit ordinary Julia is unchanged.

Runtime coefficients, indices and View weights are inputs, rather than captured
physical constants. Static-pattern preparation, compiled-kernel reuse and actual
call-local factor reuse are distinct observations. Installed-wheel functionality
remains pending; historical measurements
retain their original implementation identity.
